what: the fixture set the golden harness measures the rewrite against, and what each volume in it is a fixture of

registry.read: the application's own library, folded newest-per-slug exactly as internal/bundle.Registry folds it
registry.note: the library holds many builds per volume; the fixture is the build that would serve, and its stamp is recorded here so a re-capture that picks a different build is visible immediately
registry.exception: bend-or is the one volume not read from the library. It was built for this fixture by the reference tree's own pipeline -- tools/crawl, tools/tiles, tools/generate, unchanged since the golden-reference tag -- into a directory outside the library, and captured from there through the same internal/bundle fold. Its provenance is under the volume's builtFor.

volumes.title: TUNIC
volumes.verifiedBy: one world, one lens, one pyramid, no merge beyond its own origin account and no split sheet: the simplest shape the pipeline writes, and the fixture a change to composition breaks first.

volumes.title: Cyberpunk 2077
volumes.verifiedBy: the world payload's merge ledger names Piggyback as the origin and IGN Wiki as a donor, with 270 matched pairs, 37 added and 61 held; its second lens is an aligned resample of the donor's raster. Verified against the ledger, not assumed.

volumes.title: Fallout: New Vegas
volumes.verifiedBy: thirteen worlds, eight of them insets carrying parent=mojave-wasteland: the sheet-splitting path, and the only fixture where a volume's worlds sort by family rather than by title.

volumes.title: Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
volumes.verifiedBy: one world with three lenses carrying shards 1783, 1784 and 1785 -- the sky, surface and depths of one ground, offered one at a time. The candidates first proposed for this slot (ghost-of-tsushima, sonic-frontiers, marathon) carry no shard on any lens; this is the only sharded volume in the library.

volumes.title: Mars
volumes.verifiedBy: the one volume declaring atlas.geometry.surface=sphere, with an equirectangular mapping and two lenses over one ground (Viking MDIM and MOLA elevation). Every pin carries true planetary coordinates.

volumes.title: Bend, Oregon
volumes.classification: public city: a rendered basemap lens, curated municipal layers, and the national hydrography enrichment with HUC12 membership
volumes.verifiedBy: one world -- the capture day, which is how a city versions -- over one basemap lens rendered offline from the city's own vector data, and ten collections that no other fixture has between them: 104 paths and 44 areas carrying inline geometry, 88 of those shape features carrying atlas.hydro.huc12 from the subwatershed join, the four USGS national layers declaring atlas.label.policy=quiet, and 65 pins under a standard icon resolved by convention (atlas.icon.std=maki/monument). The survey still classifies it plain -- one world, one lens, no shard, no split sheet -- because what makes it a city fixture is its collections, not its traits.

builtFor.why: the city slot could not be filled from the library: the only city installed there is a personal location whose name stays out of the repository. This volume was built for the fixture from the public proof city in internal/arcgismap's own table, by the same pipeline that fills the library, and captured from where it was built rather than from the library.
builtFor.note: the capture day is part of the identity: the day is the world slug, the basemap tile-set path, and the bundle's version. A re-crawl on another day is another world, not this fixture.

translators.aligned: one archived capture per source, chosen to be the capture the fixture volumes were composed from

captured.note: captured from the city archive the bend-or volume was built from, not from the library's archive: arcgismap.Translate refuses a city it is not curated for, and the archive beside the library holds only the personal city. The command is `go run ./golden/capture/translators -archive <archive> -out golden/fixtures` against that same archive.

measure.verbatim: measure/maturity.txt, the report tools/maturity prints over a registry holding exactly the committed fixture set
measure.structured: measure/<slug>.build.json, internal/measure's own Build with the figures the reports derive from it
measure.defects: measure/NOTES.md -- annotated there, never corrected in the output

http.recorded: the headless application (ATLAS_HEADLESS=1) serving a registry holding exactly the five game and planet volumes -- the set as it stood before the city joined it
http.cityGap: the transcript predates bundles/bend-or and does not sample it. Re-recording the six-volume registry is one run of golden/capture/http, and it moves the range request and the eight refusals onto bend-or, which sorts first: additional coverage at the cost of re-spelling exchanges already pinned, so it is left for whoever owns the HTTP replay gate to decide.
normalized: the catalog's bundlesDir, which is where this machine keeps its library
